newsitem.title: FRANCE: Iraq buys French wheat with oil revenue.
newsitem.headline: Iraq buys French wheat with oil revenue.

text.p: Iraq on Thursday bought at least 100,000 tonnes of French wheat at a price equivalent to around $150 per tonne fob, European grain traders said.

Iraq had tendered for 100,000 tonnes of French wheat for January and February shipment, using money raised through the export of crude under a United Nations oil-for-food deal. One grain trader said the quantity actually purchased in the private tender could be as high as 200,000 tonnes.

Traders said there was also talk that Iraq was buying extra wheat in Argentina, but no deals had been confirmed. The Argentine government said last week it thought exporters had placed 80,000 tonnes of wheat with Iraq, though traders said further deals were becoming difficult as Argentina was losing a recent competitive edge against Europe.
Iraq has begun selling crude under a deal with the United Nations to raise money for relief to ordinary Iraqis hit by sanctions imposed for its invasion of Kuwait in August 1990.
France, which has lent conditional support to Iraq's calls for a complete halt to economic sanctions, is expected to be benefit from a range of oil and grain deals.
French grain firms have said initial deals could lead to more purchases to meet Iraq's needs, which Baghdad estimates at two million tonnes of commodities including mainly wheat.
